```{r fxns, include = FALSE}
escape_html <- function(x) {
  as.character(htmltools::htmlEscape(x, attribute = TRUE))
}

make_href2 <- function(url, text) {
  sprintf('<a href="%s">%s</a>', escape_html(url), escape_html(text))
}

process_wrapper_entry <- function(dat) {
  data.frame(
    Package = dat$name,
    Vignette = make_href2(url = dat$link, text = dat$title),
    Reference = make_href2(url = dat$reference, text = dat$citation),
    Source = make_href2(url = dat$source, text = dat$source)
  )
}

vignette_entries <- function(vdat, category) {
  categories <- vapply(vdat, function(x) x$category, character(1))
  index <- match(category, categories)
  if (is.na(index)) stop("Unknown vignette category: ", category)
  vdat[[index]]$vignettes
}

make_vignette_card_section <- function(vdat, cat) {
  cat('<div class="tutorial-grid">\n')
  for (entry in vignette_entries(vdat, cat)) {
    link <- if (grepl("^https?://", entry$name)) {
      entry$name
    } else {
      paste0(entry$name, ".html")
    }
    image <- if (is.null(entry$image)) {
      ""
    } else {
      as.character(htmltools::tags$img(
        class = "tutorial-card-image", src = entry$image, alt = "", loading = "lazy"
      ))
    }
    cat(sprintf(
      paste0(
        '<article class="tutorial-card">',
        '<h3 class="tutorial-card-title"><a href="%s">%s</a></h3>',
        '%s',
        '<div class="tutorial-card-body">',
        '<p>%s</p>',
        '<a class="btn btn-primary tutorial-card-link" href="%s">GO',
        '<span class="tutorial-link-context">: %s</span></a>',
        '</div></article>\n'
      ),
      escape_html(link), escape_html(entry$title), image,
      escape_html(trimws(entry$summary)), escape_html(link), escape_html(entry$title)
    ))
  }
  cat('</div>\n')
}
```

```{r yaml, include = FALSE}
library(yaml)
vdat <- read_yaml(file = "vignettes.yaml")
```

These tutorials and analysis walkthroughs introduce common workflows in Seurat.

- _You can refer to the documentation for Seurat functions [here](../reference/index.html)._
- _For vignettes from Seurat <= v4, see the [archive](archive.html)._

# Core workflows

For new users, we suggest starting with a guided walkthrough of a dataset of 2,700 peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs) made publicly available by 10X Genomics. This tutorial implements the major components of a standard unsupervised clustering workflow including QC and data filtration, calculation of high-variance genes, dimensional reduction, graph-based clustering, and the identification of cluster markers.

```{r results='asis', echo=FALSE, warning=FALSE, message = FALSE}
make_vignette_card_section(vdat = vdat, cat = "Core workflows")
```

# Seurat v6 <img src="assets/new_icon.png" class="new-icon" alt=""> {#seurat-v6}

We highlight the new features and improvements introduced in Seurat v6.

```{r results='asis', echo=FALSE, warning=FALSE, message = FALSE}
make_vignette_card_section(vdat = vdat, cat = "Seurat v6")
```

# Data integration

We provide methods for integrated analysis of single-cell datasets generated across different conditions, technologies, or species.

```{r results='asis', echo=FALSE, warning=FALSE, message = FALSE}
make_vignette_card_section(vdat = vdat, cat = "Data integration")
```

# Multimodal analysis

We also implement a suite of statistical methods for analyzing multimodal single-cell data. These include methods to integrate modalities that are simultaneously measured in the same cells, modalities that are measured in different cells, and techniques to analyze pooled CRISPR screens.

```{r results='asis', echo=FALSE, warning=FALSE, message = FALSE}
make_vignette_card_section(vdat = vdat, cat = "Multimodal analysis")
```

# Large datasets

Seurat supports analysis of datasets with millions of cells without loading the full datasets into memory. Sketch-based workflows analyze a representative subset of cells in memory, while the full dataset remains on disk. The [BPCells R package](https://bnprks.github.io/BPCells/) (Greenleaf Lab) provides efficient storage and analysis of on-disk data.

The vignettes below demonstrate sketch-based clustering and integration, reference mapping, and working with BPCells.

```{r results='asis', echo=FALSE, warning=FALSE, message = FALSE}
make_vignette_card_section(vdat = vdat, cat = "Large datasets")
```

# Spatial analysis

We provide support for the analysis of data from different spatial technologies, including sequencing-based and imaging-based methods.

```{r results='asis', echo=FALSE, warning=FALSE, message = FALSE}
make_vignette_card_section(vdat = vdat, cat = "Spatial analysis")
```

# Additional workflows

The vignettes below feature other commonly used functionality in Seurat, addressing questions that we frequently receive from users.

```{r results='asis', echo=FALSE, warning=FALSE, message = FALSE}
make_vignette_card_section(vdat = vdat, cat = "Additional workflows")
```

# SeuratWrappers

In order to facilitate the use of community tools with Seurat, we provide the SeuratWrappers package, which contains code to run other analysis tools on Seurat objects. We encourage package developers interested in interfacing with Seurat to check out our contributor guide [here](https://github.com/satijalab/seurat.wrappers/wiki/Submission-Process).

```{r results='asis', echo=FALSE, warning=FALSE, message = FALSE}
library(knitr)
vignettes <- vignette_entries(vdat, "SeuratWrappers")
dat <- data.frame(Package = character(),  Vignette = character(), Reference = character(), Source = character())
for (v in 1:length(x = vignettes)) {
  dat <- rbind(dat, process_wrapper_entry(vignettes[[v]]))
}
cat('<div class="wrapper-table">\n')
print(kable(dat, format = "html", escape = FALSE, row.names = FALSE))
cat('</div>\n')
```
